Summary: Technical Assistance to the Commission for the Assessment of Harmonised Standards. Description: This procurement ensures the continuity and strengthening of the Harmonised Standards (HAS) Consultants system, which provides the European Commission with technical and administrative assistance to perform its legal duties under Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012. HAS Consultants verify whether draft and final harmonised standards (or parts thereof) developed by CEN, CENELEC and ETSI under Commission standardisation requests comply with those requests and the relevant Union harmonisation legislation—so that the conditions for citing their references in the Official Journal of the European Union are met in accordance with Article 10(6). The need is reinforced by Court of Justice case law. The James Elliott ruling confirmed the legal effects of harmonised standards and the Commission-s duty to perform systematic controls before OJ citation, anchoring legal certainty for market actors and authorities. Building on this, the Court-s Grand Chamber judgment of 5 March 2024 in Public.Resource.Org & Right to Know v Commission (case, C-588/21 P) held that harmonised standards that generate legal effects may be subject to public access under Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001 due to an overriding public interest in disclosure, while not generally negating copyright protection. This heightens expectations on transparency, consistency and the auditable quality of compliance assessments underpinning OJ publication. Description: The European Commission is launching a study on the potential use of communication-oriented LEO constellations for the deployment of a complementary PNT service. This approach is normally referred to as Fused PNT. This tender will focus on developing a user terminal prototype and a simulated environment enabling to assess the performance of Fused PNT under a realistic set of propagation conditions and inter-satellite interference. In this procurement, the main goals of the European Commission are: • To develop a software receiver, supporting acquisition and tracking of 3GPP reference signals for Non-terrestrial networks (NTN) • To model multipath channel and intersatellite interference, in order to test the software receiver under the realistic satellite based propagation channel and interferences; • To consolidate and complement the part of the E2E emulator, by adding multipath and intersatellite interference models; • To demonstrate the performance of fused PNT ranging in a representative simulated environment • To validate the acquisition and tracking performance in realistic environment. <br> Doc Title: Fused PNT Analyses based on European Infrastructure <br> Contract Type: services. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE, YOUTH AND MEDIA. Summary: Research into the Perception of Young People at Music Events Regarding Safety, with a Specific Focus on Girls and Lgbti+ Young People. Description: This assignment concerns a current and in-depth analysis of the contemporary (music) event culture for young people in Flanders, with a special focus on the barriers to organizing events by young people themselves and on the other hand. safety perception of girls, young women and people from the LGBTQI+ community. The remarkable decline in visitor numbers and the increase in barriers to organizing something yourself make clear the need for research into underlying causes. This qualitative research will question young people themselves, as well as local authorities, youth work and other youth associations. In addition, recommendations for policy and local actors are made. This research is an update and deepening of the Party research 2002 and 2013. The final report of the Party investigation from 2013 can be found in the appendix. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE, YOUTH AND MEDIA. Summary: Research into the Underlying Mechanisms of Lgbti+ Phobia and Gender Stereotyping Among Young People in Flanders. Description: This assignment fits within the Flemish equal opportunities policy plan 2026-2029, and more specifically within main objective 6: 'We increase the well-being and acceptance of LGBTI+ people.' Despite Flanders' relatively high score in terms of legal protection and social acceptance, LGBTI+ people continue to face exclusion, discrimination and violence in various areas of life. In addition, the prevention of gender-based violence remains a point of attention. There has been the last few years a noticeable increase in homophobia and a more rigid perception of gender roles among young people. This phenomenon appears to be related to a broader societal increase in anti-GBTI+ rhetoric and the rise of the manosphere and the femosphere. The JOP monitor1 and the research 'Enoeg - enough - assez' 2 map a disturbing evolution: • 18.3% of young people find aggression against LGBTI+ people acceptable (compared to 7.4% in 2018). • 92.6% of LGBTI+ young people surveyed reported at least one form of verbal or psychological violence. • 67.4% have experienced at least one form of sexual violence. • Boys show an increasing tendency to subscribe to strict gender roles, and the influence of online communities such as the manosphere contributes to reinforce stereotypical and discriminatory ideas. This evolution has consequences for the well-being of LGBTI+ young people and girls, such as more reports of physical and psychological violence and.... Published Date: 2025-10-25. Closing Date: 2025-11-26. Competition: ICB. Financier Name: Self Financed

input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE, YOUTH AND MEDIA. Summary: Labor Market Research Into Business and Supporting Profiles in the Circus Sector. Description: The circus sector is in full development. With a view to sustainable growth, it is important in this phase to give further professionalization plenty of opportunities. This is a clear goal of the circus decree of 1 March 2019. Existing research into the socio-economic and labor market situation within the circus sector it became clear that we have little research and data about business and supporting profiles in the Circusveld. The Department of Culture, Youth and Media therefore wants to have a quantitative and qualitative research carried out that provides insight into the labor market of these supporting workers within the circus sector. The research wants to check which competencies are present within the sector and whether the competencies present match the needs of the field. If there is no agreement, it wants to check what the possible causes and associated solutions of this mismatch can be. The results of this study want to use the department to adjust the current circus policy in order to support the further professionalization of the sector sustainably. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG ENER - ENERGY. Summary: Database, Monitoring and Research on Renewable Energy Auctions. Description: In the current context, auctions and tenders for public support to renewable energies are evolving rapidly. At EU level, changes in legislation have been agreed (Electricity Market regulation) and the Commission has issued recommendations and guidance on auction design to Member States. In addition, the Net Zero Industry Act has introduced provisions regarding the use of non-price criteria in such auctions. In the current practice, zero support auctions have become more common, non-price criteria are being increasingly used and technology-specific and hybrid auctions have become part of the toolbox, while the emergence of PPA markets also provides an alternative or complementary route to the financing of renewable energy deployment. In this changing landscape, decision makers in the EU and in the Member States need a clear reference point to source and exchange up-to date knowledge about the evolution of renewable energy auctions. The overall objective is to improve the effectiveness and cost-efficiency of these tendering procedures, taking into account the EU-s decarbonisation objectives. The project will: - Collect, organise, continuously update and make publicly available relevant data on renewable energy auctions in the form of a comprehensive free online auction database; - Provide empirical and theoretical analysis and concrete recommendations regarding the key aspects of the evolution of practice in renewable energy auctions, in particular all specific design features .... Published Date: 2025-08-29. Closing Date: 2025-10-10. Competition: ICB. Financier Name: European Commission

input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG DEFIS - DEFENCE INDUSTRY AND SPACE. Summary: Fused Pnt Analyses Based on European Infrastructure. Description: The European Commission is launching a study on the potential use of communication-oriented LEO constellations for the deployment of a complementary PNT service. This approach is normally referred to as Fused PNT. This tender will focus on developing a user terminal prototype and a simulated environment enabling to assess the performance of Fused PNT under a realistic set of propagation conditions and inter-satellite interference. In this procurement, the main goals of the European Commission are: • To develop a software receiver, supporting acquisition and tracking of 3GPP reference signals for Non-terrestrial networks (NTN) • To model multipath channel and intersatellite interference, in order to test the software receiver under the realistic satellite based propagation channel and interferences; • To consolidate and complement the part of the E2E emulator, by adding multipath and intersatellite interference models; • To demonstrate the performance of fused PNT ranging in a representative simulated environment • To validate the acquisition and tracking performance in realistic environment. <br> Doc Title: Fused PNT Analyses based on European Infrastructure <br> Contract Type: services. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG MOVE - MOBILITY AND TRANSPORT. Summary: Study on Seafarer-S Fatigue and its Relationship with Working Rosters on Ferries. Description: The objective of this comprehensive study is to methodically examine the issue of fatigue among seafarers working in various functions and capacities on ferries operating between ports of an EU Member State, between EU Member States and ports between EU and non-EU countries. Recognizing the central role of maritime safety, this research will examine how fatigue, influenced by different working rosters, impacts the well-being, performance, and safety of seafarers. Fatigue among seafarers not only poses a significant threat to their health and safety but also expose the safe operation of ferries, possibly leading to maritime accidents. This study should adopt a holistic approach, considering all elements that contribute to seafarers' fatigue, such as long working hours, insufficient rest periods, irregular shift patterns, and the demanding nature of work onboard on the ship. The primary focus, however, will be on the impact of working rosters on the fatigue levels of seafarers. By analyzing different roster schedules, including those with varying lengths and frequencies of shifts, the study should aim at to identifying patterns and correlations between specific roster configurations and the incidence of fatigue-related symptoms among crew members. The study should integrate biomedical measurements tools to assess the fatigue if possible. The goal of this study is to provide evidence-based insights that can feed policy initiatives, promoting enhanced seafarer well-being and ensu.... Published Date: 2025-08-04. Closing Date: 2025-08-18. Competition: ICB. Financier Name: European Commission

Description: The objective of this framework contract is to assist EDA in implementing its Core Task 5, as defined in the EDA-s Long term review 2024. The EDA-s Core Task 5 consists in consolidating and promoting EU Member States- Ministries of Defence (MoD) common interest towards EU wider policies, both civilian and defence related. EDA contributes to promoting a shared understanding of the legal, technological, and defence challenges to benefit all Member States, industry and EU bodies and agencies. EDA thus contributes to implement current and future strategies and policies, striving to reflect appropriately MoD-s views. This contract aims to support a continuous monitoring and awareness of wider policies affecting the EDTIB, in a fast pace evolving security, policy and economic environment. The overarching goal of this framework contract is to help EDA develop and refine tools and instruments that will support the development of the EDTIB. Description: A growing number of Carbon Capture Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) projects are on track to become operational before 2030. The Communication on Industrial Carbon Management emphasises the importance of aggregating these industrial-scale projects into a knowledge-sharing platform to facilitate the collection of and information on best practices between CCUS projects in the EU. This procurement is expected to establish and operate an open collaboration and knowledge sharing platform, providing data and up-to-date information about the entire CCUS sector, based on the collection of primary data from current and future large-scale demonstration projects. Description: Decarbonisation of international shipping is high on the agenda of the European Commission, with the Smart and Sustainable Mobility Strategy calling on the IMO to strive for high standards in the field of climate change. IMO adopted a number of measures to reduce GHG emissions from international shipping : the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII), the Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) the Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP), the Data Collection System (DCS), the Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI). A GHG Fuel Standard and an economical measure (so called Mid-term measures) must be adopted in 2025 for international shipping to reach the goals set in the revised IMO GHG Strategy (2023). A revision of the CII framework must be further considered at IMO after MEPC 83 and potentially of the EEXI and EEDI frameworks as well. Guidelines will need to be developed to implement the mid-term measures, as well as the SEEMP and the DCS. Additionally, the IMO has adopted and advanced guidelines on the life cycle GHG intensity of marine fuels (LCA Guidelines). Efforts are ongoing to refine and finalize these guidelines, including certification frameworks and addressing technical and sustainability aspects. The LCA framework will support the implementation of Mid Term Measures and need to be further developed to effectively inform and support the regulatory framework. Description: Decarbonisation of international shipping is high on the agenda of the European Commission, with the Smart and Sustainable Mobility Strategy calling on the IMO to strive for high standards in the field of climate change. A GHG Fuel Standard and an economical measure (so called Mid-term measures) must be adopted in 2025 for international shipping to reach the goals set in the revised IMO GHG Strategy (2023). A revision of the CII framework must be further considered at IMO after MEPC 83 and potentially of the EEXI and EEDI frameworks as well. Guidelines will need to be developed to implement the mid-term measures, as well as the SEEMP and the DCS. Additionally, the IMO has adopted and advanced guidelines on the life cycle GHG intensity of marine fuels (LCA Guidelines). Efforts are ongoing to refine and finalize these guidelines, including certification frameworks and addressing technical and sustainability aspects. The LCA framework will support the implementation of Mid Term Measures and need to be further developed to effectively inform and support the regulatory framework. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG MOVE - MOBILITY AND TRANSPORT. Summary: Study on Seafarer-S Fatigue and its Relationship with Working Rosters on Ferries. Description: The objective of this comprehensive study is to methodically examine the issue of fatigue among seafarers working in various functions and capacities on ferries operating between ports of an EU Member State, between EU Member States and ports between EU and non-EU countries. Recognizing the central role of maritime safety, this research will examine how fatigue, influenced by different working rosters, impacts the well-being, performance, and safety of seafarers. Fatigue among seafarers not only poses a significant threat to their health and safety but also expose the safe operation of ferries, possibly leading to maritime accidents. This study should adopt a holistic approach, considering all elements that contribute to seafarers' fatigue, such as long working hours, insufficient rest periods, irregular shift patterns, and the demanding nature of work onboard on the ship. The primary focus, however, will be on the impact of working rosters on the fatigue levels of seafarers. By analyzing different roster schedules, including those with varying lengths and frequencies of shifts, the study should aim at to identifying patterns and correlations between specific roster configurations and the incidence of fatigue-related symptoms among crew members. The study should integrate biomedical measurements tools to assess the fatigue if possible. The goal of this study is to provide evidence-based insights that can feed policy initiatives, promoting enhanced seafarer well-being and ensu.... Published Date: 2025-06-11. Closing Date: 2025-08-11. Competition: ICB. Financier Name: European Commission

Description: KCE has been tasked with the scientific evaluation of a new financing system for home nursing care, which will be tested in a number of pilot practices. Summary: Comparative Study on Best Practices for a Stronger Eu Sanction Enforcement. Description: Restrictive measures (sanctions) are an essential tool for the promotion of the objectives of the Common Foreign and Security Policy. Their objectives include safeguarding the Union-s values, maintaining international peace and security, consolidating and supporting democracy, the rule of law and human rights. The sanctions remain the main instrument in the Union-s toolbox to deter, prevent and condemn aggressive and illiberal behaviour of the third countries. Considering that the lack of sanction implementation, as well as inconsistencies across different jurisdictions of the Union, also represent a risk to Union financial interests and to the national financial systems, it is important to make sure that the Union sanctions are implemented equally across the Union. This is particularly relevant for the implementation of the Union sanctions against Russia, which have been subsequently adopted starting from 2014. In order to curb circumvention of Union sanctions and assist the Member States in their sanction implementation tasks, this pilot project concerns a study on the best practices and synergies that would benefit the Union-s sanction policy, taking stock of the examples of the United States- Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) and the United Kingdom sanctions enforcement authority (OFSI). Summary: Comparative Study on Best Practices for a Stronger Eu Sanction Enforcement. Description: Restrictive measures (sanctions) are an essential tool for the promotion of the objectives of the Common Foreign and Security Policy. Their objectives include safeguarding the Union-s values, maintaining international peace and security, consolidating and supporting democracy, the rule of law and human rights. The sanctions remain the main instrument in the Union-s toolbox to deter, prevent and condemn aggressive and illiberal behaviour of the third countries. Considering that the lack of sanction implementation, as well as inconsistencies across different jurisdictions of the Union, also represent a risk to Union financial interests and to the national financial systems, it is important to make sure that the Union sanctions are implemented equally across the Union. This is particularly relevant for the implementation of the Union sanctions against Russia, which have been subsequently adopted starting from 2014. In order to curb circumvention of Union sanctions and assist the Member States in their sanction implementation tasks, this pilot project concerns a study on the best practices and synergies that would benefit the Union-s sanction policy, taking stock of the examples of the United States- Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) and the United Kingdom sanctions enforcement authority (OFSI). This would help to identify similarities, disparities, best practices and missing elements across all the jurisdictions of the Union. Considering that each Member State nominates.... input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG EMPL - EMPLOYMENT, SOCIAL AFFAIRS AND INCLUSION. Summary: Eu Fair Transition Observatory (Efto). Description: The Council Recommendation on ensuring a fair transition towards climate neutrality was adopted by the Member States in June 2022, as integral part of the ‘Fit for 55- package. The Council Recommendation provides policy guidance to Member States on how to address the employment and social aspects of the transition and also outlines the commitment of the Commission to strengthen the knowledge base for policymaking and public debate related to fair transition. To date, numerous stakeholders have called upon the Commission to advance and strengthen the EU-s just transition framework. In this context, this upcoming call for tenders seeks proposals for the establishment of an EU Fair Transitions Observatory in 2024. The Observatory is expected to facilitate the monitoring and implementation of fair transition policies across the EU, at all levels and involving key stakeholders, in different domains beyond coal intensive regions and sectors. It will provide up-to-date information on fair transition policies, showcase best practice examples promoting fair transitions and strengthen the evidence base on fairness aspects of the transition through the collection and provision of relevant data and analytical work. <br> Doc Title: EU Fair Transition Observatory (EFTO) <br> Contract Type: services. Summary: Study of Barriers to the Consolidation of and Reduced Fragmentation in Trading and Post-Trading Infrastructure. Description: The purpose of this lot is to explore barriers to consolidation of trading and post-trading infrastructure and potential ways to address those barriers identified. The assessment of the barriers should take into account vertical, horizontal and other types of consolidation among trading and post-trading infrastructure as well as explore the role that technology could play in removing those barriers. The assessment should also identify and characterise the synergies and operational cost reductions resulting from past consolidation.
